section: Preamble - text, keywords, 42nd Amendment; is the Preamble part of the Constitution (Berubari, Kesavananda)
subsections: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: With reference to the amendability of the Preamble, which one of the following correctly describes the position laid down in Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)?
o: The Preamble can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament without constitutional limitations.
Only the President can amend the Preamble with the approval of the Supreme Court.
The Preamble cannot be amended under any circumstances.
The Preamble can be amended under Article 368, but its basic features cannot be destroyed.
accepted.x: Kesavananda Bharati held that Parliament can amend the Preamble under Article 368, but cannot alter or destroy its basic features.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between amendability and the basic-structure limitation.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preamble has been amended only once so far.
2. The amendment of the Preamble was made in 1976.
3. The amendment inserting new words into the Preamble was made through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Preamble was amended only once, through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical clue and verify whether all linked details refer to the same amendment.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly explains the significance of the Supreme Court’s decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) in relation to the Preamble?
o: It removed secularism from the list of basic constitutional principles.
It declared that Parliament could not amend any part of the Preamble.
It reaffirmed secularism as a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
It held that secularism became a constitutional principle only after the 42nd Amendment.
accepted.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) reaffirmed that secularism is part of the Constitution’s basic structure. A State government acting against this principle could be dismissed.
accepted.tq: Identify the case associated with reaffirmation of a constitutional principle rather than with the original amendment.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: With reference to a State government acting against the principle of secularism, which one of the following is correct in light of S.R. Bommai (1994)?
o: It could not be subject to any constitutional consequence because secularism is only a political ideal.
It could be removed only by the Supreme Court and not by constitutional authorities.
It could be dismissed for acting against a basic-structure principle.
It could be dissolved only by a constitutional amendment.
accepted.x: S.R. Bommai reaffirmed secularism as part of the basic structure, and a State government acting against it could be dismissed.
accepted.tq: Apply the case-law principle to an institutional scenario and identify the constitutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: The basic-structure review of constitutional amendments made after which date was specifically associated with Waman Rao (1981)?
o: 26 November 2015
24 April 1973
18 December 1976
26 January 1950
accepted.x: Waman Rao (1981) held that basic-structure review applies to amendments made after 24 April 1973.
accepted.tq: Recall the legally significant cut-off date and distinguish it from the dates of later amendments or observances.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional sequence of adoption is correct?
o: The Preamble was enacted only after the 42nd Amendment so that it matched the amended Constitution.
The Preamble and the rest of the Constitution were adopted simultaneously without any difference in sequence.
The Preamble was adopted before the rest of the Constitution so that all later provisions conformed to it.
The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had been adopted so that it matched the constitutional text.
accepted.x: The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had been adopted, so that it matched the final constitutional text.
accepted.tq: Test sequence and purpose together; the trap is reversing the order of adoption.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: In Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India, decided on 25 November 2024, the Supreme Court is stated to have—
o: struck down the insertions made in the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment.
upheld the words ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to their insertion.
directed Parliament to conduct a fresh referendum on the Preamble.
held that the Preamble could never be reviewed by the judiciary.
accepted.x: On 25 November 2024, the Supreme Court upheld ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to the 42nd Amendment insertions.
accepted.tq: Use the case-name and date to distinguish the latest judicial position from earlier constitutional debates.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the relationship between the 1976 insertion of the word ‘Secular’ and the basic structure doctrine?
o: Secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word was inserted in the Preamble.
The 42nd Amendment removed secularism from the basic structure and retained it only in the Preamble.
Secularism was excluded from the Constitution until the Supreme Court recognised it in 1994.
Secularism became part of the basic structure only because the word was inserted in 1976.
accepted.x: The constitutional position stated in the material is that secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word was inserted in 1976.
accepted.tq: Separate the textual insertion of a word from the pre-existing constitutional principle it expresses.
accepted.sec: Amendability of the Preamble - case and limits

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a criticism of the insertion of certain words into the Preamble during the Emergency?
o: The insertions were made without a fresh popular mandate.
The insertions were made after a referendum expressly rejecting those words.
The insertions were made by the Supreme Court without parliamentary approval.
The insertions were made before the Constitution was adopted.
accepted.x: A criticism was that the words were inserted during the Emergency without a fresh popular mandate.
accepted.tq: Identify the criticism without confusing it with the counter-view defending the constitutional principle.

accepted.s: The counter-view in the debate over the insertion of ‘Secular’ in the Preamble is that—
o: secularism was introduced into the Constitution only by the 42nd Amendment.
the Preamble has no relationship with constitutional principles concerning religion.
Articles 25 to 28 deal exclusively with emergency powers and not religious freedom.
secularism was always inherent in the Constitution, including through Articles 25 to 28.
accepted.x: The counter-view is that secularism was inherent in the Constitution even before the insertion of the word, with Articles 25 to 28 cited in support.
accepted.tq: Link the interpretive argument to the constitutional provisions expressly associated with it.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court has upheld the continued presence of ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble.
2. The decision arose in the context of the 75-years-of-the-Constitution debate.
3. The Court rejected challenges to the insertions made by the 42nd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Supreme Court upheld the words and rejected challenges to the 42nd Amendment insertions in the context of the contemporary constitutional debate.
accepted.tq: Combine the judicial holding, the constitutional debate, and the challenged amendment before selecting the code.

accepted.s: Constitution Day in India is observed on which date, and since which year has it been observed in this form?
o: 26 January, since 1950
26 November, since 2015
24 April, since 1973
15 August, since 1947
accepted.x: Constitution Day is observed on 26 November, and it has been observed since 2015.
accepted.tq: Pair the date with the year rather than selecting a familiar national day or constitutional milestone.
